notable_absence.finding: THIS IS THE KEY FINDING FOR THE STATE-VOCABULARY QUESTION. A page titled 'Index Lifecycle' describes creation, building, updating and scanning in detail and names not one single state. No 'created', no 'building', no 'online', no 'ready', no 'deferred' as a state value, no 'pending', no 'scheduled for creation', no 'Active', 'Warmup' or 'Paused'. It has PHASES with actors and ordering ('Index creation happens in 2 phases'), where the promoted registry has STATES with values (index-state for an index, indexer-node-state for the Index Service on a node). The two vocabularies describe the same span of an index's life and this page reconciles them nowhere - it does not say that the creation phase corresponds to any state, nor that a deferred index reports one. So the answer to the brief's second question, from this page, is: still not settled, and now with a documented reason why - the lifecycle documentation and the state enums were written in different vocabularies by different hands. Also absent: any mention of DROP, so the 'lifecycle' this page describes has no end; and any state or phase for a FAILED build, though the creation phase 'validates the user input' and so can evidently reject it.

cross_component_finding: Four internal inconsistencies. (1) Two consecutive bullets in Index Scans name the same setting twice with different words: 'If the index consistency is `not_bounded`' then 'If the scan consistency is `at_plus` or `request_plus`'. The registry promotes n1ql:scan-consistency; 'index consistency' is this page's own coinage, and it is also the anchor text of the page's last link ('[Index Consistency](index-replication.md#index-consistency)'), so the alias is load-bearing, not a one-off slip. (2) The DCP stream scope changes between sections without acknowledgement: at build time 'The projector requests a DCP stream on the specified collection' and 'DCP streams only the documents in the collection'; at update time 'The projector keeps a bucket-level DCP stream open'. A reader who took the build-time diagram literally would conclude wrongly. (3) The page introduces three named internal components - projector, indexer, scan coordinator - with no definitions and no links to any page that defines them, in a document aimed at readers planning their data structure. (4) It swaps unit words mid-page: indexes are on collections, but deferring is justified by not 'having to re-scan the entire keyspace for each index', and 'Creating and building indexes can take a long time on keyspaces with lots of existing documents'. Collection and keyspace are used interchangeably in the same paragraph.
cross_product_finding: This page is the counter-case to indexing-and-query-perf.md three files away in the same Capella directory. Here: 'collection' thirteen times, 'keyspace' twice and only in the deferred-build aside. There: 'keyspace' fifteen times, 'collection' never. Both are Capella pages, both are about GSIs, and the registry's gloss on server:keyspace ('the term the server/ tree uses where the Capella tree says collection') fits neither reliably. The split is per-page, not per-tree, and probably per-author. Phase 2 should treat capella:collection and server:keyspace as one referent with two live spellings inside Capella, not as a tree dialect. Second cross-product observation: the page's only definitional link for DCP goes out of the Capella tree into server/current, and the component vocabulary it uses (projector, indexer) is server-internal architecture that no Capella page defines - so a Capella-only reader cannot resolve the terms this page depends on. Third: three of the four components and phases minted here (projector, indexer, scan coordinator) are exactly the kind of thing the promoted indexer-node-state enum presupposes, which suggests the registry's node-state enum was promoted from a server page that named these components while this Capella page names them without any state at all.
